findings.message: the pattern matches 4 of 5 sample lines. It must match every one: a line it misses is dropped entirely, not partly parsed. The first it misses is '[12] Oct 25 15:14:25 Login attempt for nonexistent user from 172.21.55.93:55370'. Of the 7 patterns, the closest to it is '^\\[%{INT:pid}\\] (?<timestamp>%{MONTH} +%{MONTHDAY} %{TIME}) Child connection from %{IP:client_ip}:%{INT:client_port}$'. the pattern matches up to %{IP:client_ip}, which fails on '] Oct 25 15:14:25 Login attempt for none'. The capture before it, %{INT:pid}, matched only '12' and stopped at '] Oct 25 15:' - it is too narrow, and that is the one to widen. That position does not hold a bare number If this line is a VARIANT of the others - an extra word, a field that is sometimes absent - make that part optional with (?:...)? rather than writing a second pattern. If it is a DIFFERENT KIND of message - different words, not one more of them - add a pattern for it to `alternatives`, reusing the same capture name for the same value.

findings.message: scenario r5_tomcat_json__holdout_01: the detection rule expected 5 matches but found 0. the documents carry source.ip but never http.request.method. Those fields are declared in the mapping and absent from the output, so either the source key does not exist or the extraction is not reaching it.

scenario r5_tomcat_json__holdout_02: the detection rule expected 3 matches but found 0. the documents carry http.response.status_code but never http.response.body.bytes. Those fields are declared in the mapping and absent from the output, so either the source key does not exist or the extraction is not reaching it.

scenario r5_tomcat_json__holdout_03: the detection rule expected 1 matches but found 0. the documents carry user.name but never url.original. Those fields are declared in the mapping and absent from the output, so either the source key does not exist or the extraction is not reaching it.

scenario r5_tomcat_json__holdout_04: the detection rule expected 1 matches but found 0. 6 document(s) were produced and NOT ONE of them carries any of the fields the rule needs (user_agent.original). The mapping may well be right; the parser is not producing these fields. Check `extraction` first - if the layout is wrong, every field is empty and every rule fails regardless of where it is mapped.
the probe injected 'GET' as http.request.method, and it appears in no field of any parsed document. The parser dropped it.

the probe injected '9927' as http.response.body.bytes, but the parser put it in http.response.bytes. Whatever the source calls that key, its value is http.response.body.bytes - that is what the probe did.
the probe injected 'HTTP/1.1' as http.version, and it appears in no field of any parsed document. The parser dropped it.
the probe injected '/missing.jsp' as url.original, and it appears in no field of any parsed document. The parser dropped it.

the probe injected 'Mozilla/5.0 Firefox/128.0' as user_agent.original, and it appears in no field of any parsed document. The mapping reads user_agent.original from 'request.requestHeaders.User-Agent', so that key is not being extracted from the line: check `extraction`.
